notes: The client IP revert that v0.4.93 claimed to fix is actually fixed. That patch promoted a row to a reservation only when the request carried no ip_type, reading a named ip_type as "the admin chose this" -- but the client edit dialog puts ip_type into the payload on every save, unconditionally, so the guard excluded exactly the path every real user takes and the code never ran outside its own tests. Reported again unchanged after upgrading: 20.20.255.209 changed to 20.20.2.3, saved, reverted. A deliberate choice is now the narrower thing it should always have been -- a row that is currently static being switched to dynamic. Any other hand-typed address is a reservation. The regression test uses the dialog's exact payload and fails against the v0.4.93 condition. Also fixed: NAT not working after an update until you opened a session and pressed save. Boot restore kept runtime_ifname for sessions still dialled, then immediately systemctl restarted those same sessions and threw it away -- pppd killed at 17:58:28, ppp0 back at 17:58:29, and the nftables generator ran inside that gap, building the ruleset while ppp0 did not exist and skipping every DNAT rule. Boot restore now leaves a dialled session alone; an admin's own apply still restarts everything, since new peer files and credentials only take effect once pppd comes back. Those systemctl calls no longer block either, so a port with no cable in it cannot stall the restore for 40 seconds behind start-pre.
